activity.role: Queen mother and royal political actor
activity.notes: The Pazarcik boundary-stone inscription names Sammu-ramat as the palace woman of Shamshi-Adad V and mother of Adad-nirari III, and records her crossing the Euphrates with Adad-nirari during the 805 BCE intervention in Kummuh. ATLAS records that securely attested political-military appearance only; it does not assert a formal regency or import the later Semiramis legends.

sources.title: Two Neo-Assyrian Stelae — Annual Review of the RIM Project
sources.citation_text: The Pazarcik stele translation identifies Sammu-ramat as palace woman of Shamshi-Adad V, mother of Adad-nirari III, and records Adad-nirari and Sammu-ramat crossing the Euphrates in the intervention commemorated by the boundary stone.

sources.title: Shalmaneser III, king of Assyria — Nimrud: Materialities of Assyrian Knowledge Production
sources.citation_text: ORACC notes that Sammu-ramat wielded considerable political power, joined the Assyrian army on campaign, and had a stela inscribed in her name and displayed at Assur.
